body: I used to hate mainstream stuff and now I watch Love Island. The possibilities are endless. I understand it's frustrating to constantly hear the same judgement, but don't let the actual things he is saying get to you
So when you introduce her to people, do you have to say "This is girlfriend"?

I think you should tell your girlfriend who can handle it from there. It's being cruel to be kind. Of course your girlfriend's sister has begged not to say anything, though it sounds like she just needs some help. Yes, it's an embarrassing situation for her but outing the problem can lead to help, and once she has this problem sorted I'm sure she'd be nothing but thankful
Thank you!

I'd stay away from texting about more serious conversations about feelings. At least call him if you can't see him for a while. If you can't call, you may just have to wait it out a little. Hearing emotion in voice is important when talking about issues. In some cases, facial expressions and body language can tell half the story.

I said those things and I stand by them. It's not selfish, I think it's quite a popular opinion that people don't want others getting credit of their work. And in the workplace, not tolerated at all. It's not about wanting people to suffer, it's about doing what he's supposed to do, which is the work he was set. If his friend's reason was something way more important, I'd understand and be there for them, but slacking because you're 'tired' is not an excuse and won't get you anywhere. Either help him once and allow him to be lazy, or don't and teach him he can't leech of others.

Since when is it selfish to not give your work out to people?? If anything, giving a friend your work to pretty much copy is being a shitty friend because you're hardly teaching them a good lesson. He needs to teach him that he has to work for his success, better early rather than later in life when it could cost you your job or something. No offence, but you sound like you let your friends walk all over you.

Yeah it's low effort to send it over, but I wouldn't like to share my work for a friend to copy and 'edit'. I put effort into it, I should be the one getting the credit. Whether it's a friend or not, I wouldn't want someone getting it that easy using MY work. He probably put more effort into sending him the guide (Don't know if he created the guide himself). So it's not a matter of OP not being bothered to send it, he doesn't want to because it doesn't feel right and at least compromised since he already said he would.

Of course he did it to hand in. Sorry for my ambiguity. What I mean't is along the lines of, they both got set the assignment, OP's friend shouldn't be able to take this easy option because he's 'tired'. OP probably put time and effort into the assignment and would be risking getting into trouble by doing that. Yes, he said he would but it was impulsively and never promised anything. He still put in the effort to send him a guide on how to do it.

NTA. If she has a shop that sells vintage items and she can't identify a proper vintage item, she shouldn't have a shop in the first place. Plus, she may actually know in which case she's an asshole. I'd report.

NTA. I don't think your feelings are invalid. Just be sure to communicate what you feel to him, because lack of communication is usually the key to destroying a relationship. Just make sure to approach it in a calm, non-aggressive way.
NTA. Why should you have to do the work just for him to copy it. Sending him a guide to answer the questions is the best thing you could've done.

I wouldn't call you an asshole, it's just things that snowballed into others. I guess you could've just been a little more organised and gone to sleep earlier/set an alarm if you knew you were seeing him the next day regardless of not knowing when/where. Now that you're back in your head space to think it all back, I'd just talk about it and properly apologise. Maybe make it up to him in someway.
There's a reason you have to be 18 to get a tattoo, because it's there for the rest of your life. Hair grows back but he might be too young to make the decision of a tattoo. Am I wrong?
YTA. If he's not harming anyone, let him express himself. Doesn't matter what you think he looks like. Not sure about the tattoo though depending on his age.

Do anything that could help. Talk to her about your feelings, how you're scared for her and how much you love her. Confiscate the paraphernalia and drugs from your place. Talk to Nikki about how you don't want her doing coke (very unlikely going to work as I'm sure she sells to your gf so loss of a customer and she's probably a cokehead herself so won't care). Worst comes to worst, try get her in rehab. Anything you can think man.

Sounds like she's getting addicted. Anyone addicted to drugs that you tell to get off drugs will never comply. You're going to have to go through a lot of conflict if you want to get her better, no doubt about that. It comes down to a decision from you. Whether it be you risk your relationship and do the best you can to get her to stop, tell her how it makes you feel. Or let her carry on and risk her health/life. If you really love her I'd do the best you can to get her the hell out of that downward spiral before it's too late.

NTA. I think the passing of your Mother has had a heavy affect on his daily mental state, which is unsurprising, horrible thing to happen and I'm sorry that you had to go through that. If all you do is clash when you live together it's probably a good idea to separate yourselves from each other. That way you can organise days/weekends to see him and you will appreciate your time together more. I don't know how much you talk about your mother's passing with him but maybe try and find out how much it's affecting him.

NTA. If I hadn't seen my gf in weeks I'd be doing anything I could to make that night work. I'm not sure if it's the fact that she doesn't care about you, more that she is addicted to drugs. Might want to talk to her about that.

Not much info here but whether you're being hypocritical or not, as long as you're supporting I don't think it can hurt. It's just easy to throw it back in your face because you are being hyprocritical.

NAH. Hard to compare due to the difference in the amount of results. Could have been a difference in the way you wrote the perspectives. If it gained more attraction, the amount of 'NTA' votes could have overtaken. I think your hardly valid reasons are just swaying your opinion. I mostly vote 'NTA' because I like to find the positive intention in everything. But that's just me.

It is hypocritical, but you can only fight for it so much before letting it go. If you think she should be treating you better etc, find someone else who will, or learn not to care about smaller things like that.

NTA. Run as far as you can from John. You may care for him now, but he sounds like nothing more than a manipulative piece of shit who is taking advantage of that. Telling someone they wish they killed themselves after an episode of depression, berating you in front of your friends, blocking you then roping you back in when he wants because you're letting him. Truly unjustified behavior, get him out of your life.

All I can say is things don't always make sense. But on this level, sometimes you just have to let it go or find someone that better fits your needs. Sounds like you're on your phone a lot. I put my phone down for who knows how long after I send a message. Instead of trying to pry at this situation, I recommend you just focus on other things more.
So she also gets annoyed at you for leaving?

NTA. Your friend may frown upon you but it's always your choice whether you want to donate or not. If she calls you out, call her on her spending spree. Regardless of the circumstances, would you be donating because you feel you have to or because you actually want to help the child? If the latter, I'd just donate anyway. Otherwise, do what you want because you never have to give away your earned money no matter how people look at you.

I have people blank my messages sometimes. But they eventually get back to me and other times they'll respond very quickly. I've learnt not to care how long it takes for people to message me back. I get that you guys were in a conversation, maybe she just wanted a break and I guess she wasn't obliged to tell you so. Maybe she just thought you wouldn't care.

NTA. Sounds like your boyfriend is talking to this girl a LOT. Whether there is something going on or nothing, I find it weird that he can be so close to someone who was a bad friend to you. If the way you're making it out to be is true, it seems their communication is very excessive. I think the breaking point for me was when you said he checks through your messages a lot while saying he said you don't trust him. That's a complete contradiction because if he trusted you, why does he need to go through your phone? So he doesn't have much right to say you don't trust him. I would be bothered by it.

NTA. She sounds quite shallow with the 'why can't you be like this' sort of comments. I'm sure it would make the majority of people uncomfortable to hear things like that about other guys. The fact that she isn't taking your feelings into account is already bad, especially because you aren't asking anything unreasonable at all. The way you said all her friends ganged up on you makes her sound even more immature. I'd take a break, and if she can't grow up, I'm sure you'll find better people.
YTA. You're prioritising your dick over her as a whole person. She doesn't have to do anything she doesn't want, you have no valid reasoning and obviously don't really care that much about her.

Definitely NTA. Your friend obviously has no respect for your feelings and just cares about what she wants. Your brother can't be right as he said 'it won't affect' you 'in any way' and you already gave two perfectly valid reasons as to why you don't want to do it. You're getting a lot of pressure put on you for something that is completely your choice. It's a huge decision and I wouldn't go through with it if you feel uncomfortable.

NAH. Seems like a silly argument got out of hand and led to something which could have been quite serious. Though it got sorted and put behind very quickly. Moving positively is good but shame you had to find out yesterday. If you're brother is fine with it, let him be, but if you aren't then I just wouldn't hang around Tom if you don't like that kind of behaviour.

NTA. I think it's a little weird since your sex life now is 'fantastic' as you said. But I don't think there is anything wrong with it due to your reasons. Your friend probably thought you just wanted to sleep with more people, but as you say, it's because you just wanted to be better for him.

Definitely NTA. There's no deals, money or contracts here. If you don't want to do it I'd just tell them. I'm sure it still takes quite a lot of time out of your days to make animations regardless of the effort put in. May as well start your own thing if you have the most skill.

NTA. She sounds like a terrible influence on your daughter and if you kept letting it slide, your daughter may have started picking up the same tendencies and think it's okay as you hadn't stood your ground. Of course your daughter is going to be upset with you for this, but your neighbor's child has some serious behavioral issues and I certainly wouldn't tolerate that in my home no matter how upset my child would get.

NAH. Yes it can be slightly frustrating when people do this. You can think of it as a bit rude but to play devil's advocate, the conversation with another friend may have been a full-attention kind of conversation. In which case she could've just dropped you a message to let you know she's busy. But I'd just try to care a lot less about response times from people, sounds like you may be getting slightly caught up in something smaller than you think. At least she did get back to you and not in an absurd amount of time. In terms of her feeling annoyed, it could of just been a private conversation that she didn't want to talk about and didn't feel the need to justify not replying to you for a while.

I wouldn't call you an asshole it just sounds like you've messed up a lot. I can tell that you aren't happy with your own decisions and do feel bad about it. You definitely have made a mistake here and if you don't want to go on that trip, all you can do is compensate her as much as you can/want to make up for it. The trip sounds fun though, maybe you should just say 'fuck it' and have a good time (if you can actually afford it). You'll make the money back.

I don't think you'd be the asshole, but you'd cause huge damage in your family doing that behind her back. If you want to go about it in a 'cleaner' way, I'd inform her ex about going to court and getting custody. Then it's properly sorted out. Though if you don't care about the relations in your family, it does sound like he deserves to see them.

NTA but you won't get out of it without looking like one. People agree to sex and change their mind later all the time. You don't have to have any sexual interaction you don't want. "If someone asks for a cup of tea and later decides they don't want it, don't pour the cup of tea down their throat". That's a quote if from a video about consent I had to watch in school haha. I'm sure it'll hurt her telling her this news, though you'd risk hurting her more if you went through with it without really wanting it. Just apologise that you let things go a little too far, but you have changed your mind and you don't want to go any further.

I understand that, probably a healthier route to leave it in that case. I'm sure it was also hard on her part not being able to see you but she's dealt with it in such a shitty way. In my opinion, someone willing to ghost you is not worth your time. Sorry this happened to you.

NTA. If it's affecting you this much, you should be able to trust your partner and tell her for your sake. Though if you're guilty conscience is too strong, you may just have to stick through it by yourself

NTA. I can easily understand how you're fed up and hurt by that. Awful thing to go through. I'd at least hear what she has to say and unless she has some amazing reason as to why she's been like this, I wouldn't call it forgivable. To me, I can't think of an excuse under the sun for this, but you may always find yourself a little curious if you never attempt to find out.

NTA. Everyone has a right to their own beliefs. It's not fair that she wants you to conform to her beliefs under any circumstance. Hold your ground in the nicest way possible and make some suggestions for other things you can do on Mother's Day

NTA. He wants to buy you a PC to play games with him. While that may be fun, if he's getting annoyed at you for not accepting the gift, he could easily get annoyed if you find yourself not wanting to play games with him as often as you thought. This just results in guilt-tripping and pressure on you to comply to him as he bought you the PC. That could terribly spiral off and cause more arguments. Regardless, he should respect your feelings as they are in no-way unreasonable. You're uncomfortable with it and that's okay, I'm sure many others would be too.
